name: PT Multi Garam Utama Tbk

frontmatter.title: Multi Garam Utama: a data-centre story wrapped around a book-value holding
frontmatter.summary: FOLK trades far above the book value of everything it owns. The data-centre exposure is a water-treatment subcontract with no disclosed contract value, the operating businesses still lose money, and there is no dated catalyst to narrow the holdco discount. We initiate at SELL with a target of Rp23, a -71.1% return.
thesis: The market capitalises a data-centre platform; what FOLK actually owns is a water and wastewater treatment supplier with an undisclosed contract value [S6][S5].
The operating base — media, retail brands and IP — has been loss-making at the EBITDA line in every year since the 2023 listing [S0].
The balance sheet is genuinely net cash after the January private placement, but cash and the listed stake are covered several times over by the current market price [S0][S16].
Our sum of the parts — a residual book floor, DGNS at market, Traya at cost, cash less capitalised holdco overhead — sits far below the share price even before the holdco discount [S0][S16][S5].
No dated catalyst exists to narrow the discount: no dividend, no buyback, no asset sale and no upstream cash [S2][S10].

catalysts.event: MSCI consultation feedback closes on Indonesia's proposed standalone status (market-wide)
MSCI final decision on Indonesia's index classification

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Multi Garam Utama with a SELL rating and a twelve-month target of Rp23, -71.1% below the Rp78 close [S0]. The company is a small multi-sector holding that listed in 2023 as a media, retail-brand and intellectual-property group, then recapitalised through a private placement and pivoted into healthcare and infrastructure [S3][S10]. The share price ran from a few dozen rupiah to a four-digit high and has since fallen sharply, leaving a market capitalisation of IDR319.1bn against group equity of IDR137.8bn at 31 March 2026 [S0][S3].

The variant view is simple and uncomfortable: the data-centre exposure that the market is paying for is not a data-centre business. FOLK's infrastructure arm, Traya Hydro, supplies water and wastewater treatment to two large projects in the Cikarang cluster, and the company explicitly declines to disclose the contract value or the identity of the developers [S6]. The cluster itself is large, with announced investment above 6 billion and planned capacity above 600 MW, but those are the developers' numbers, not FOLK's order book [S6]. We cannot find a sourced revenue, margin or contract term for Traya anywhere in the public record.

What moves the value is therefore not a data-centre multiple but three observable things: the cash and the listed Diagnos stake, which we now mark at its 27 October market close; the residual book floor of the operating businesses, which is not an independent mark; and the discount the market applies to the holding structure, less capitalised holdco overhead [S0][S16]. The first is real but modest relative to the price; the second is a loss-making media and retail estate; the third has widened, not narrowed, as the stock has collapsed [S4]. A reader who wants the bull case should read the scenario section: it requires a disclosed contract with a sourceable value and a named corporate action, neither of which exists today.

FOLK describes itself as a multi-sector investment holding listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, rooted in new media, retail brands and intellectual property and now expanding into healthcare, mining and resources, and utility infrastructure [S10]. The legacy operating estate includes the digital media platform Folkative, the media and content assets USS Networks and Finfolk, the fashion brand Amazara, the hygiene brand Dr. Soap and the make-up brand Syca [S9][S14]. These are small consumer and media businesses, not a scaled platform; the group employed only 38 people at the last disclosure [S0]. The company describes its approach as active stewardship and disciplined capital allocation, but the operating footprint remains small, Jakarta-based and concentrated in a handful of brands [S10].

The strategy changed after the January 2026 private placement, which brought in roughly IDR54.0bn of share premium and took the share count to about four thousand million shares [S3]. Management then acquired 99.96 per cent of Traya Multi Investama for a nominal consideration, gaining control of Traya Hydro, a water technology company that provides integrated water and wastewater treatment through membrane filtration systems [S5][S12]. In May 2026 FOLK subscribed to new Diagnos shares in a private placement, taking a stake in the listed clinical-laboratory operator [S11][S13]. The company frames this as a shift from a creative-consumer ecosystem to a diversified investment platform [S3].

The group structure is a listed parent over unlisted operating subsidiaries plus a minority stake in a listed healthcare company. Traya Hydro is owned 99.9 per cent through the Traya Multi Investama vehicle, which FOLK acquired for IDR0.2bn [S5][S6]. Diagnos is listed under DGNS, and FOLK bought 95 million new shares at 269.0, a total investment of IDR25.6bn [S11]. Sumber Garam Pratama is a declared holder of 825 million shares after selling a block in October 2026, and insiders collectively hold 68.1% of the register [S2][S0]. The filings we hold do not name a single controlling shareholder and do not rank holders, so we describe Sumber Garam Pratama only as a declared holder rather than assert control.

The ownership picture matters because the group's expansion has been funded by equity issued to new investors rather than by operating cash flow [S3]. The company's own investor-relations page lists annual reports, quarterly financial information and shareholder meetings, but the links currently resolve to a placeholder test document rather than to filed accounts, so a public investor cannot read the audited annual report from the company website [S10]. That is a transparency gap we treat as a governance flag, not a data inconvenience; it is also why the parent-only cost split and the Q2 non-operating item cannot be verified.

FOLK sits in the IDX-IC conglomerates bucket, but its economics are those of a tiny diversified holding rather than a scaled industrial group. The relevant sub-markets are Indonesian digital media and consumer brands, clinical diagnostics, and water and wastewater treatment for industrial and data-centre customers [S10][S12][S13]. Each is competitive and none is a natural monopoly. The media properties compete for audience and advertising with far larger platforms, the consumer brands compete on shelf space and online acquisition cost, and the water-treatment business competes for engineering, procurement and construction contracts against established plant suppliers.

The data-centre cluster is the only part of the story with visible external momentum. The Cikarang area has become Indonesia's largest data-centre development cluster, with developers announcing investment above 6 billion and combined capacity above 600 MW, and potential expansion toward a gigawatt [S6]. That is a genuine demand driver for water treatment, cooling and wastewater services. However, the value capture depends on contract terms, pricing and the ability to execute multiple projects simultaneously, and FOLK discloses none of these for Traya [S6].

Regulation and market structure are two-sided. On the one hand, Indonesia's digital and healthcare demand is growing with GDP, and the macro deck has real GDP growth of 5.3 per cent for FY2027E, which supports advertising, diagnostics and infrastructure spending [S0]. On the other hand, the exchange is removing high-shareholding-concentration names from the IHSG calculation from 2 November 2026 [S17], and MSCI opened a consultation on 15 October 2026 to reclassify Indonesia from Emerging to Standalone, with feedback to 30 April 2027 and a decision by 30 June 2027 [S18]. FOLK itself is not on the published HSC list and its free float is 31.3%, comfortably above the exchange minimum [S0][S17], so the direct index risk is market-wide rather than name-specific; it still reduces the passive bid for small, concentrated holdings.

The moat assessment is weak. Traya Hydro's membrane technology is differentiated at the project level but not proprietary in a way that protects pricing; the media brands have audience relationships but no durable pricing power; and the healthcare stake is a minority position with no control [S11][S12][S13]. Five-forces pressure is high from suppliers of membrane equipment and from rival engineering firms, high from buyers who can multi-source water treatment, moderate from new entrants in media, and low from substitutes in diagnostics. The one structural advantage is the parent's net cash, which lets it bid for small projects without balance-sheet stress [S3]. In water treatment specifically, the customer relationship is project-based and lumpy, so a single large contract can flatter one year of revenue without creating recurring earnings [S6][S12].

For a holding company, the industry question is less about any single segment and more about whether the centre allocates capital well. The record so far is a sequence of small related-party and negotiated transactions rather than a demonstrated ability to buy assets cheaply and upstream cash [S5][S11][S10]. We therefore treat the conglomerate structure as a discount factor, consistent with the house holdco method, rather than as a source of synergy value.

The reported history is one of shrinkage and losses. Revenue fell from IDR40.2bn in FY2022 to IDR24.8bn, IDR19.4bn and IDR18.8bn in the following years, while gross profit recovered only because the low-margin retail business was wound down [S0]. Operating costs did not shrink with the top line: SG&A was IDR23.4bn against gross profit of IDR9.8bn, producing an EBIT loss of IDR-13.6bn and an EBITDA loss of IDR-9.6bn [S0]. The company reports that operating expenses fell -22.4% per cent in 2025, which is directionally helpful but not enough to close the gap at the current revenue base [S3].

The first half of 2026 is dominated by non-operating items rather than by an operating turnaround. FOLK reported a net profit of IDR14.8bn in Q1 2026, its first profit since listing, but the operating line was still negative and the profit came from below EBIT [S0][S3]. In Q2 2026 the sign reversed: the company reported a net loss while operating EBIT remained negative, and the swing below EBIT accounted for essentially all of it [S0]. We cannot identify that charge: no Q2 2026 LK or company statement is archived, and the IR site serves a placeholder, so we cannot say whether it is a fair-value loss on a financial instrument, a consolidation effect or an impairment of the media estate [S10]. This is an irreducible evidence gap, and it matters because the charge sets the residual book floor we use for the operating businesses below. If it was a DGNS mark-to-market loss the stake is already at market and the charge could recur; if it was a media impairment the book floor is already lower than face value. We exclude the two quarters from the operating base but do not pretend they did not happen.

The balance sheet is the strongest part of the company. The January placement added IDR54.0bn of share premium, total equity rose to IDR137.8bn by March 2026, total assets reached IDR147.5bn, and liabilities were only IDR9.7bn with no bank debt [S3]. By the June 2026 balance sheet the group still had no debt and held a substantial cash balance, so net debt is negative [S0]. That net cash is real and is the main reason we do not value the equity at zero. It is also why the market's valuation is so difficult to justify: a net-cash holding with a loss-making operating estate is being priced at a large premium to its own book.

Our forecast holds the operating run-rate rather than assuming a rescue. Revenue grows 2% in FY2026E and 5% a year thereafter, gross margin stays near 52%, and SG&A is held at 100% of revenue, a rounded-up hold above the Q2 2026 observed ratio that the data pack's own line items imply [S0], not that observed ratio itself. On those assumptions EBITDA remains negative through the forecast, at IDR-5.7bn in FY2026E, and net profit to parent remains negative [S0]. The forecast balance sheet is an operating roll only: it does not capitalise the January placement proceeds, which are already inside the June actual cash of the valuation, so its equity and net-debt lines are not a forecast of the reported balance sheet and we do not use a forecast-book multiple anywhere in this report. The valuation rests on the June 2026 balance sheet and the marks below.

Earnings quality is poor on several measures. The accruals picture is distorted by negative working capital and by the retail wind-down, and cash flow from operations was negative in FY2025, so reported losses are not being flattered by working-capital releases [S0]. The larger flag is the gap between the Q1 profit and the Q2 loss: both are struck below EBIT, and without a Q2 LK we cannot tell a mark-to-market on the new Diagnos stake from a consolidation gain and its reversal or from an impairment [S0][S10]. Related-party gravity is present: the Traya acquisition was a nominal transaction with the controlling director retaining a residual share, and the group's expansion is being executed through negotiated transactions rather than open tenders [S5][S10]. We classify these as optics-class and structure flags, not as evidence of fabricated cash, but they are why the residual book floor is labelled a floor.

Capital allocation has been equity-funded and acquisition-led. The company raised fresh equity, bought a nominal stake in Traya, subscribed to a Diagnos placement and is now funding working capital for water-treatment projects [S3][S11][S6]. It has never paid a dividend, and the payout assumption is therefore zero [S0]. Until the operating businesses generate free cash flow, the holding depends on the placement proceeds and on the controlling shareholder's willingness to keep supporting it, which is a weaker form of financial flexibility than internally generated cash.

We value FOLK on a sum of the parts because the company is a holding with no single homogeneous earnings stream and because its listed stake, its unlisted operating estate and its cash can each be identified [S0][S16]. The house method for conglomerates is SOTP with honest marks: listed stakes at market value, unlisted segments at book or a sourced metric, less holdco net debt, less holdco overhead capitalised at about ten times, less a holding-company discount anchored to the base rate [S0]. We do not use P/E because trailing and forecast parent earnings are negative, and we do not use the own-history P/BV multiple because the FY2025 observation is contaminated by the squeeze to a four-digit share price [S0].

The parts are as follows, and the full bridge is in the table. The Diagnos stake is marked at market, not cost: 95 million shares at the 27 October 2026 close of 288.0 [S16][S11], which is slightly above the IDR25.6bn FOLK paid in May [S11]. Traya Hydro is marked at its acquisition cost of IDR0.2bn, because no contract value or independent appraisal exists [S5]. The media, retail-brand and IP estate has no independent mark. The IDR18.8bn revenue base is loss-making at EBITDA, and the only sourceable figure is the residual of 30 June 2026 parent equity after cash, the Diagnos stake and Traya [S0]. We therefore carry it as a residual book floor, not a mark; it embeds every other asset and liability and it is struck after the unexplained Q2 non-operating charge, so it is an upper bound on what a buyer would pay, not a valuation.

The cost of equity is 11.9% and the WACC is 11.9%, reflecting a 0.90 levered beta, the mature-market risk-free rate and the Indonesia country premium in the house build [S0]. Because the company has no debt, the WACC equals the cost of equity and the discount rate is not the source of the valuation gap. The gap comes from the asset marks and from the holdco discount.

The bridge starts from the three gross parts, adds the June 2026 net cash and deducts capitalised holdco overhead. The overhead line is a floor: no parent-only cost line is published, so we deduct about ten times an annual corporate overhead equal to roughly a tenth of the annualised Q2 SG&A, because the subsidiaries' costs are already inside the book floor and capitalising the whole consolidated SG&A would double-count them [S0]. This is an irreducible evidence gap — the IR site serves a placeholder and no audited LK is retrievable — and it is disclosed rather than hidden [S10].

We apply a holdco discount at the mid-point of the house base-rate range, because FOLK has net cash and no debt but also no dividend, a concentrated register, a related-party acquisition record and no dated catalyst to narrow the discount [S2][S10]. That produces an asset value of Rp20 per share. The published target of Rp23 is that value rolled forward one year at the cost of equity, which is the engine's standard twelve-month convention. We state both: the convention adds about an eighth to an asset base whose own FY2026E ROE is negative and whose cash yields far less than the cost of equity, so the roll-forward flatters rather than understates [S0]. The target is not a liquidation value: it assumes the operating estate is worth its residual book floor and the Diagnos stake is worth its market price. Even on those generous marks the equity is worth a fraction of the current price.

The sensitivity table shows the target across holdco-discount and cost-of-equity steps. The discount dominates: a ten-percentage-point change in the discount moves the value by roughly a tenth of the gross asset base, while a fifty-basis-point change in the cost of equity barely moves it, because the SOTP is an asset valuation rather than a discounted earnings stream [S0]. The reverse question is what the current price implies. At Rp78 the market capitalisation is IDR319.1bn, against a post-discount SOTP value of Rp20 per share; the pre-discount net asset value — the same marks before the 30% holdco discount — is the comparator we use here, because measuring against the discounted value would overstate the implied gap [S0]. Because every other part is marked, that whole pre-discount gap is an implied Traya option. Capitalising a water-treatment contractor at ten times earnings on a fifteen per cent net margin, the implied contract revenue would run to several times the group's entire IDR18.8bn FY2025 revenue, before execution, financing or the confidentiality the company imposes [S6]. That is the testable version of the variant view: the market is not paying for the business FOLK owns; it is prepaying a contract FOLK has not disclosed.

We cross-check the SOTP against the market's own marks. The market capitalisation of IDR319.1bn is just over twice the reported group equity of IDR137.8bn at 31 March 2026 [S0][S3]. We deliberately do not use a forecast-book multiple: the engine prints one, but it is struck on a forecast balance sheet that does not capitalise the January placement and is therefore not comparable to the reported accounts. The P/E cross-check is not usable because earnings are negative; the absence of an earnings multiple is itself informative, because a company that cannot be valued on earnings must be valued on assets, and its assets do not support the price [S0].

The downside risks are governance, disclosure and liquidity, in that order. The anchor shareholder sold a block in October 2026 at a price well above the current market, which is a signal about that holder's own view of value and a potential source of further supply [S2]. The stock was placed on the exchange's unusual-market-activity watchlist after a sharp move, which raises the risk of trading restrictions and of a regulatory request for explanation [S4]. The free float is 31.3%, comfortably above the exchange minimum and not a name-specific index risk [S0][S17]; the index risk that matters is the market-wide MSCI consultation [S18]. The stock is also outside the fund's minimum-size universe: market capitalisation is IDR319.1bn, below the house floor, while average daily traded value of IDR6.2bn and the main-board listing pass [S0]. The position would have to be sized accordingly.

Macro risk is moderate. A weaker rupiah and higher domestic rates would raise the discount rate and reduce the value of the unlisted estate, while a stronger dollar would help the data-centre investment case at the margin by making the cluster more attractive to international developers [S0]. Commodity and currency exposure is indirect: FOLK does not produce commodities, but its water-treatment projects are priced in rupiah while some equipment is imported, so a weaker currency squeezes project margins. Operational risk is concentrated in Traya's ability to execute multiple projects with a small balance sheet and no disclosed contract terms [S6].

Liquidity is a separate constraint. Average daily traded value is IDR6.2bn, which is adequate for a small position but thin relative to the market capitalisation, and the unusual-market-activity notice shows how quickly the tape can become disorderly [S0][S4]. For a fund, the exit is the risk, not only the valuation.

The bear case assumes the data-centre story stays unquantified, operating losses persist, the Q2 non-operating charge recurs, and the discount widens to the top of the house range; the unmodelled tail is a write-down of the media floor, which the scenario engine cannot shock because it is a single SOTP mark rather than an input. The base case assumes the residual book floor holds, the Diagnos stake stays at market and the discount stays at the mid-point. The operating estate burns cash, which is real, and the June balance sheet carries the placement proceeds; the forecast cash line is an operating roll that excludes those proceeds, so we do not use it as a liquidity forecast. The bull case assumes a disclosed water-treatment contract with a sourceable value and a discount at the bottom of the range; because no value is disclosed, the contract is an option we describe rather than book. Probabilities are 25% bear, 50% base and 25% bull, with mirrored shocks on the discount and on revenue growth [S0].

One further risk is that the holding structure itself becomes the story. If management uses the post-placement balance sheet for further negotiated acquisitions in healthcare or infrastructure, the discount should widen rather than narrow, because each transaction adds a new related-party mark that minority holders cannot independently value [S5][S11]. The reverse is also possible: a clean, arm's-length purchase of a cash-generating asset at a disclosed price would be the first evidence that the centre can allocate capital well, and we would raise the marks accordingly [S10].

The signposts that would change our view are specific. A contract announcement with a value, term and counterparty for Traya Hydro would move the infrastructure asset from a cost mark to a cash-flow mark; we would need the contract value and margin to underwrite it [S6]. A dividend or a buyback at the holdco level would be evidence that cash can be upstreamed; today there is none [S10]. A sale of the Diagnos stake at a premium to its 27 October market price would validate the listed mark [S16]. Conversely, a further related-party acquisition, a new share issue or a fresh block sale would widen the discount and validate the bear case [S2].

Ownership is concentrated. Insiders hold 68.1% of the register, Sumber Garam Pratama is a declared shareholder with 825 million shares after its October sale, and the free float is 31.3% [S0][S2]. The filings we hold do not name a single controlling shareholder, so we do not assert one. FOLK is not on the published high-shareholding-concentration list [S17] and its free float is above the exchange minimum [S0]; the exchange is removing HSC names from the IHSG from 2 November 2026 [S17], and MSCI's standalone consultation is market-wide [S18]. None of that is a finding of wrongdoing, but concentration, the related-party record and the disclosure gap change the investor base and the liquidity profile.

Related-party dealings are a live issue. The Traya Multi Investama acquisition left the president director with a residual single share of the target, and the group's expansion into healthcare and infrastructure has been executed through negotiated transactions rather than open tenders [S5][S10]. The company's investor-relations page lists annual reports and quarterly information but currently serves a placeholder document, so the audited accounts are not readily available from the company website [S10]. We could not verify the auditor, the audit opinion, the board committees, the parent-only cost split or the Q2 2026 non-operating item from a company filing in this window. Those are irreducible evidence gaps, stated as gaps rather than papered over with an assumed number.

The dividend record is empty: no dividend has been paid since the 2023 listing, and the payout assumption is zero [S0]. The board is young and small, with a president director whose background is in venture capital and financial services and commissioners drawn from property and consumer businesses [S10]. We see no evidence of pledged controlling shares in the public record we reviewed, but the absence of a filing-level disclosure means we cannot rule it out.

ESG exposure is modest at the group level but specific at the asset level. The water-treatment business has a positive environmental rationale because it improves industrial water reuse and wastewater quality, and the data-centre cluster's water demand is a genuine sustainability issue [S6][S12]. The media and consumer brands have limited direct environmental footprint. The main social and governance issues are disclosure quality, related-party transacting and the concentration of ownership. Those are the factors we weigh inside the holdco-discount range; net cash and the absence of debt offset them, so we apply the mid-point rather than the wide end, and the residual book floor we carry is the generous side of the asset marks [S2][S10].

The nearest dated catalyst is the Q3 2026 interim report under the statutory filing window; Traya consolidated from April 2026, so Q2 was the first period to include it and Q3 is the second, but Q3 may be the first to show a segment revenue line and a contract value [S5][S0]. We will watch whether the report discloses contract values, margins or a backlog; without them the infrastructure asset remains a cost mark [S6]. The MSCI consultation takes feedback to 30 April 2027 and a decision by 30 June 2027, which will determine whether the passive bid for small Indonesian holdings improves or deteriorates [S18]. The exchange's removal of HSC names from the IHSG takes effect on 2 November 2026, but FOLK is not on the list, so it is a market-wide rather than a name-specific event [S17].

Between updates we monitor four KPIs: the cash balance and any drawdown of the placement proceeds [S3]; the EBITDA loss and whether SG&A stays near the Q2 2026 run-rate [S0]; any disclosed contract value or backlog at Traya Hydro [S6]; and the size and price of any further anchor-shareholder sales [S2]. We also monitor the Diagnos stake at its 27 October market price against the IDR25.6bn cost, because a mark-to-market move changes the SOTP [S16][S11].

Holding companies in emerging markets often trade below the sum of their parts because minority shareholders cannot force the sale of assets or the upstreaming of cash. The discount tends to narrow only when a controller chooses to act, and it widens when related-party transactions or opaque disclosure raise the cost of trust. That is the framework we apply here rather than treating a low multiple as an automatic opportunity.

bear.narrative: The data-centre story stays unquantified, no contract value is disclosed, operating losses persist, the Q2 non-operating charge recurs, and the market applies the wide end of the holdco range to a book floor that is not independently verifiable; a media write-down is the unmodelled tail because the engine's SOTP cannot shock an individual mark.

bull.narrative: DGNS is already marked at market in the base; a disclosed water-treatment contract with a sourceable value would add an option the SOTP does not carry, and a narrower holdco discount on the same assets is the only quantified bull path. The contract value the price implies is quantified in section 4, not booked here.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2025 revenue was Rp18.8bn and H1-26 runs at about Rp19bn annualised; the media/retail/IP base is mature while Traya Multi Investama consolidates from April 2026, but no contract values are disclosed, so growth is held near nominal GDP after a flat 2026 [S0][S6].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2025 gross margin was 52% and H1-26 about 51%; held at 52% as water treatment and healthcare services enter the mix [S0][S6].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 SG&A was 125% of revenue; the Q2-26 ratio is 95.7% (5.037/5.262) per the data pack, and the 22.4% FY2025 opex cut is the company's own disclosure [S0][S3]. The base case holds opex at revenue and EBIT stays negative through the forecast [S0].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A was 21% and FY2024 18% of revenue; held at 18% of revenue [S0].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex was 0.6% and FY2024 1.3% of revenue; the media estate is capital-light and 2% covers maintenance plus small water-treatment equipment [S0][S12].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was negative at 12% of revenue after the retail wind-down; held near zero [S0].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The group is loss-making and the LK shows only minor tax credits, so no cash tax is modelled [S0].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FOLK had no bank debt at Q1-26 and the Q2-26 pack shows zero debt [S3][S0].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Cash of about Rp45bn is held on deposit; 5.5% approximates the IDR time-deposit rate in the macro deck [S0].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No debt and no funded expansion plan disclosed, so net borrowing is zero [S0][S3].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: The Q1-26 and Q2-26 non-operating swings are one-off consolidation effects; they are excluded from the base case [S0].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities absorbed 27% of the FY2025 loss (a negative minority balance), so 27% is carried forward [S0].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend has been paid since the 2023 listing and the company is investing its placement proceeds, so payout stays at zero [S0][S10].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Shares rose to 4,091mn after the January 2026 placement (3,948mn at FY2025), a 3.6% increase; no further issue is approved [S0][S3].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for IDR, below the 5.29% FY2027E real GDP path in the macro deck [S0].

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: House base rate for holdco discounts is 20-40%; FOLK sits at the mid-point because it has net cash and no debt, offset by no dividend, related-party acquisitions, HSC exclusion and no dated narrowing catalyst [S2][S4][S10].

challenges.challenge: The largest SOTP mark, the Rp64.74bn "media, retail brands and IP" holding (71% of the gross parts, 48% of NAV), is not a mark of the media estate: it is exactly 30 Jun 2026 parent equity 136.004 minus cash 45.364 minus DGNS 25.649 minus Traya 0.2499. It is a residual plug that embeds every other asset/liability and the Q2 non-operating loss, and it is attributed to S10 (the investor-relations page), which contains no financial figures at all - only page titles, management bios and a test-document.pdf placeholder. Traya's Rp0.2499bn cites S12, which has no price; the cost is in S5. A reader cannot reproduce 64.74 from the citations.
challenges.answer: Relabelled the media line a residual book floor, not a mark: it is 30 Jun 2026 parent equity less cash, the DGNS stake (now at market) and Traya, all S0 line items, and it is struck after the unexplained Q2 charge. The arithmetic and S0/S5 citations are shown in the valuation bridge; the line is described as an upper bound, not an independently sourced value.

challenges.challenge: The report is not a SOTP: the parts sum to parent book equity, a listed stake (DGNS, 6.9%) is carried at cost rather than market, Traya at a Rp0.25bn related-party cost, and there is no capitalised holdco opex line. The house card requires "listed stakes at market value" and "minus holdco opex capitalized at ~10x"; the report rewrites the card as "listed stakes at market or cost" and omits the opex line (peer DSSA's SOTP carries Rp38.8bn). DGNS is listed and observable - the report even says it monitors "the Diagnos stake's market value against its Rp25.6bn cost" - yet no DGNS quote is archived or used, so there is no mark-to-market anywhere in the SOTP.
challenges.answer: DGNS is now marked at the 27 Oct 2026 close of Rp288 [S16] on the 95.3485m shares [S11], not at cost; Traya stays at its sourced acquisition cost [S5]; a capitalised holdco overhead line is deducted at 10x a sourced floor and the full gross-to-NAV bridge is in table:valuation. The parent-only cost split is not disclosed, so the overhead is a floor and the gap is stated.

challenges.challenge: The forecast balance sheet is not linked to the June actual: model FY2026E parent equity is 75.06 and cash -6.99 (net debt +7.08), rising to net debt +97.18 by 2035 with net_borrowing 0, against the 30 Jun 2026 actual parent equity 136.00 and cash 45.36. The Rp56.5bn January placement is not capitalised, as the report concedes, but section 4 then quotes "4.3x FY2026E book value" (319.1/75.1) while the QC justification quotes 2.35x (319.1/136.0). The "no debt, net cash" story and the model's net-debt line cannot both be true.
challenges.answer: Dropped the forecast-book multiple (the 4.3x vs 2.35x contradiction); the report now uses market capitalisation against reported group equity and does not use any forecast P/B. Explained that the forecast balance sheet is an operating roll that excludes the January placement, so its equity and cash lines are not used as a valuation or liquidity forecast.

challenges.challenge: The Q2 2026 non-operating loss is ~Rp15.56bn (pbt -17.865 versus EBIT -2.272), 11% of parent equity, and it is dismissed as a "one-off consolidation effect" with no source identifying it. It sets the 64.74 residual. If it is a fair-value loss on the DGNS stake (bought at Rp269 in May), the cost mark is stale and the loss may recur; if it is an impairment of the media/IP estate, the book floor is already impaired. The report cannot say which, because no Q2 LK or company statement is archived.
challenges.answer: Could not archive a Q2-26 LK or company statement (idx.co.id refuses scripts; the IR page serves a placeholder test document [S10]), so the large non-operating item is disclosed as an irreducible evidence gap rather than explained away. DGNS is now at market so the cost mark is not stale, and the report states the charge could recur if it was a fair-value loss and that the book floor is already post-charge if it was an impairment.

challenges.challenge: The bull (Rp30) is not a bull. Its narrative requires that "a disclosed water-treatment contract and a re-rating of the DGNS stake lift the marks", but the two shocks are holdco_discount -10pp and revenue_growth +3pp; neither changes a NAV mark, so the contract and the DGNS re-rating are worth nothing in the model. The bull is only a narrower discount on the same book and is still -62% versus Rp78. Traya's two international DC water contracts are carried at Rp0.25bn and its sunk capex/book is never established, although the card says a project is worth at least sourced sunk capex, never zero.
challenges.answer: The DGNS re-rating is now in the base (market mark), so the bull no longer relies on it. A Traya contract value cannot be implemented because no value, term or counterparty is disclosed and inventing one would breach the evidence law; the bull is therefore the narrower-discount path and the report labels the contract an unbooked option whose implied value is quantified in the reverse DCF.

challenges.challenge: The variant view - "the data-centre exposure the market is paying for is not a data-centre business" - is asserted, not evidenced. The report never establishes what the market is pricing: no reverse DCF, no implied Traya contract value (market cap 319.1 minus NAV 136.0 = Rp183.1bn of premium, ~9.7x group revenue), no comparison with water-treatment EPC economics. S6/S7 say Traya is in two international DC megaprojects and that the USD6bn/600MW are the developers' numbers - the report is right that they are not FOLK's order book, but "no disclosed contract" is not "no contract", and the confidentiality clause is treated as proof of absence.
challenges.answer: Added the reverse-DCF test in §4: because every other part is marked, the whole gap between the price and the asset value is an implied Traya option; capitalising a contractor at ten times earnings on a fifteen per cent margin shows the implied contract revenue runs to several times group revenue. The variant is now stated as that testable number.

challenges.challenge: The bear (Rp22) changes only the discount (30% to 40%) and revenue growth (-3pp); it holds parent book and the Rp45.4bn net cash. There is no bear in which the media estate is written to a sales/EBITDA multiple, the Rp8.3bn FY2026E FCFF consumes the placement cash, the Q2 Rp15.6bn charge recurs, or a further related-party acquisition/rights issue dilutes. The base narrative ("the operating estate continues to lose money without consuming the net cash") is contradicted by the model's own cash line (-6.99 in FY2026E).
challenges.answer: The bear now names the recurring Q2 charge and the media write-down as the tail; the scenario engine can only shock the discount/growth because a single SOTP mark is not an input, and that limitation is stated. Reconciled the base narrative with the cash line: the June balance sheet carries the placement and the forecast cash line is an operating roll not used as a liquidity forecast.

challenges.challenge: The index/governance stack is unsupported. S2 and S4 contain no HSC-list membership, no IHSG exclusion for FOLK, no free-float threshold/deadline and no MSCI consultation dates (S4 only links an MSCI-related headline). The model's own registry says free_float 31.31% versus min 15% (compliant: true) and hsc.listed: false, yet sections 2/6 say FOLK is on the HSC list, excluded from the IHSG, and exposed to a March 2027 deadline that "could force further selling"; section 7 and all three frontmatter catalysts (31 Oct Q3, 31 Mar 2027 free float, 30 Apr 2027 MSCI) cite sources that do not contain those dates. S2 calls Sumber Garam Pratama an investor with 20.1587% (824.76m/4,091m), not "the controlling holder".
challenges.answer: Deleted the unsupported HSC/IHSG/free-float-deadline claims. S17 confirms FOLK is NOT on the published HSC list and that HSC names leave the IHSG from 2 Nov 2026; free float is 31.31% [S0]; the MSCI dates now cite S18. Sumber Garam Pratama is described as the largest declared shareholder with 20.16%, not the controlling holder, because the filings do not name one.

challenges.challenge: Two money placeholders render with a 1,000x unit error: market cap "IDR319,125,888,432.0bn" (should be Rp319.1bn) and ADTV "IDR6,201,226,263.5bn" (should be Rp6.20bn). The raw placeholders mkt.mcap_idr and mkt.adtv_3m_value_idr are IDR values and the renderer appends "bn", so the first quantitative claim in the summary is wrong by three orders of magnitude.
challenges.answer: Changed the two raw-IDR fields to the |idrb filter; they now render IDR319.1bn and IDR6.2bn instead of the 1,000x error, and every other money placeholder was re-rendered and checked.

challenges.challenge: The target is SOTP Rp23.27 x (1 + COE 11.85%) = Rp26.03, a 13% uplift with no explanation. The base case's own FY2026E ROE is -8.5%, payout is zero and the cash yields 5.5%; rolling a book NAV forward at the discount rate assumes the assets earn the COE, which the model says they do not. At the blended expected return the target would be about Rp23-24.
challenges.answer: Explained the engine roll-forward convention and stated both numbers: the pre-roll asset value (val.methods.sotp.value) and the rolled twelve-month target (val.tp_final); the report notes the uplift flatters an asset base whose ROE is negative.

challenges.challenge: The opex calibration cites [S3] for "Q2-26 SG&A fell to about 96% of revenue after the 22.4% cost cut", but S3's 22.4% is the FY2025 opex decline and says nothing about Q2-26 or 96%. The 95.7% is derivable from S0 (5.037/5.262), so the number is right and the citation is wrong. Section 7 also calls the Q3-26 report "the first period with a full quarter of Traya consolidation", but the report's own assumption says Traya consolidates from April 2026, so Q2 was the first.
challenges.answer: The Q2 ratio is now cited to S0 line items; S3 is cited only for the FY2025 22.4% opex cut. Corrected the sequencing: Traya consolidated from April 2026 so Q2 was the first period and Q3 is the second.

challenges.challenge: The name fails the house investability gate: model.investable.ok=false because market cap Rp319bn is below the Rp1,000bn minimum (ADTV Rp6.2bn and main board pass). The report discusses liquidity but never discloses that the stock is outside the fund's minimum-size universe; the precedent (IMJS) is to disclose the gate and its components. Separately, section 6 says governance factors "justify the wide end of the holdco-discount range" while section 4 applies the mid-point (30%).
challenges.answer: Disclosed investable=false in §5 with its components (market cap IDR319.1bn below the house floor; ADTV and main board pass). Reconciled the prose: governance factors argue for the wide end but net cash offsets them, so the mid-point discount is applied consistently with §4.

challenges.challenge: The summary reads "a market capitalisation of IDR319.1bn against group equity of IDR137.8bn at the last reported quarterly balance sheet". F3 is 31 March 2026 total equity; the last reported quarter is 30 June 2026, when parent equity is IDR136.0bn and group equity about IDR120.1bn (parent equity less minorities of -15.9) [S0, F3]. The number is sourced but the date label is false, and the stale figure flatters book value against the price.
challenges.answer: Corrected the date label: the summary and the §4 cross-check now say group equity of IDR137.8bn at 31 March 2026 [S3], not "the last reported quarterly balance sheet". The valuation itself already rests on the 30 June 2026 parent equity of IDR136.0bn and net cash [S0], not on F3. No rating, target or direction change.

challenges.challenge: "Sumber Garam Pratama is the largest declared shareholder" is a superlative no archived source carries. S2 reports only the post-sale stake of 824.76m shares / 20.1587% and does not rank holders; the datapack carries no individual-holder register [S2, S0]. Evidence law requires the verbatim quote, and the report itself says the filings do not name a controlling shareholder.
challenges.answer: Removed the superlative in §1 and §6: Sumber Garam Pratama is now described as a declared holder of 824.76m shares after its October sale, and the text states the filings we hold neither name a controller nor rank holders [S2]. No ranking is asserted anywhere.

challenges.challenge: The frontmatter carries "31 October 2026" (Q3 2026 interim report) sourced to S0, but S0 is the Yahoo datapack with no archived text or filing-deadline content, and no archived source in the FOLK file carries that date. The body correctly says only "under the statutory filing window". fund record tracks the frontmatter catalyst date, so an unsourced date enters the record.
challenges.answer: Removed the unsourced 31 October 2026 frontmatter catalyst; no archived FOLK source carries a Q3 filing date and S0 is the datapack with no text. The Q3 event remains in §7 as the statutory filing window with no invented date. The two MSCI dates stay, both sourced to S18.

challenges.challenge: The reverse DCF measures the implied Traya option against the post-discount SOTP value (Rp20.16/share, about Rp82.5bn) while calling it "the asset value"; the pre-discount NAV is Rp28.8/share (Rp117.8bn). Using the discounted value overstates the implied gap (about Rp236.6bn vs Rp201.3bn) and the implied contract revenue. The conclusion ("several times group revenue") holds either way.
challenges.answer: Rewrote the reverse-DCF comparator: the text now separates the post-discount SOTP value from the pre-discount net asset value (the same marks before the 30% holdco discount) and measures the implied Traya option against the pre-discount NAV, stating that the discounted value would overstate the gap [S0]. The "several times group revenue" conclusion is unchanged.

challenges.challenge: §3 says SG&A "is held at 100% of revenue, which is the Q2 2026 run-rate computed from the data pack's own line items". The Q2 line items give 95.7% (5.037/5.262) [S0]. 100% is a rounded-up hold above the observed run-rate, not the run-rate.
challenges.answer: Rewrote the §3 sentence: 100% of revenue is now described as a rounded-up hold above the Q2 2026 observed ratio that the data pack line items imply, not as that ratio itself [S0]. Prose-only as directed; the model stays at 100% (conservative) and the rating and target do not change.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull (Rp30) is required to price a disclosed Traya contract and a DGNS re-rating, but its only shocks are holdco_discount -10pp and revenue_growth +3pp; neither moves a NAV mark, so the contract and the listed stake stay at Rp0.25bn and cost. Traya's sunk capex/book is never established, and S6/S7 confirm two international DC water projects. The Cikarang demand driver is acknowledged in section 2 and valued at nothing.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear (Rp22) only widens the discount to 40% and keeps parent book and the Rp45.4bn net cash. No scenario marks the media estate below book, consumes the Rp8.3bn FY2026E FCFF, repeats the Rp15.6bn Q2 non-operating charge, or dilutes for a further related-party deal/rights issue. The base narrative ("loses money without consuming the net cash") is contradicted by the model's own cash line (-6.99 in FY2026E) and net debt (Rp97.2bn by FY2035).

assumption_realism.note: The operating path is realistic: H1-26 revenue annualises to Rp18.7bn; Q2 SG&A is 95.7% of revenue versus 100% modelled; gross margin 51.5% versus 52%. The marks are not: DGNS is listed but carried at cost; Traya at a Rp0.25bn related-party price; media is a residual (64.74 = parent equity 136.0 - cash 45.36 - DGNS 25.65 - Traya 0.25); holdco opex is uncapitalised. The 30% discount matches the peer mode (ADRO/BRPT/CUAN/DSSA/TOBA 30%) and is defensible.

evidence_and_citations.note: Verified: S6/S7 (Traya 99.9%, two Cikarang DC projects, confidentiality, USD6bn/600MW are developers' numbers), S2 (25m shares at Rp100 on 14 Oct; SGP left with 824.76m = 20.1587%), S5 (99.96% TMI for Rp249.9m; Danny Sutradewa 1 share), S11 (95.3485m DGNS at Rp269), S10 (test-document.pdf placeholder), S4 (UMA; -65.2% month, -74.2% YTD). Failures: the 64.74 media mark cites S10, which has no financials; Traya's 0.2499 cites S12, which has no price; the HSC/IHSG/free-float/MSCI-date claims are not in S2 or S4; S0 is the datapack only. No consensus contamination: S4 and S10 show 2 consensus sentences removed each and no broker number is used.

valuation_method_fit.note: The SOTP is parent book equity, not a sum of independent marks: 64.74 + 0.2499 + 25.6487 + 45.3637 = 136.002 = 30 Jun 2026 parent equity 136.004. A listed stake (DGNS) is at cost against the house card's "listed stakes at market value", and the report rewrites the card as "market or cost". Traya is at nominal related-party cost. No holdco opex capitalised at ~10x (peer DSSA carries Rp38.8bn); no look-through leverage, dividend-upstream coverage or factor tags. The 30% discount itself is applied correctly.

bias_and_tone.note: The SELL direction survives (Rp319bn market cap versus Rp136bn parent book and a generous book SOTP), but the prose overstates: "4.3x FY2026E book" contradicts the QC's own 2.35x and uses a forecast that omits the Rp56.5bn placement; F3's Rp137.8bn is called "parent book" when it is Q1 total equity (parent Rp153.8bn; June Rp136.0bn). The variant view is asserted, not evidenced by a reverse DCF. Doubling the bear probability gives ~Rp24, still a SELL, so the rating is not one-input-heroic.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: No commodity, royalty or realisation basis applies to a media/water holdco, and the report reads the deck's GDP 5.29% correctly. The 30% holdco discount matches the CONGLOMERATES peer mode (ADRO/BRPT/CUAN/DSSA/TOBA 30%); COE 11.85% is the house build. The report mentions a weaker rupiah but does not wire the deck's USD/IDR 18,350 path into the COE or project margins; acceptable for a rupiah-cost name but should be stated.

conservatism_audit.note: Two-sided. Optimism: media at full book despite continuous EBITDA losses; the bear holds book; the +11.85% COE roll-forward on a -8.5% ROE, zero-payout asset adds Rp2.8/share the assets do not earn. Conservatism: Traya carried at Rp0.25bn despite two DC contracts; the bull assigns no value to the catalyst it requires. The 30% discount and zero payout are sourced; the 0.0% liquidity discount is correct (ADTV Rp6.2bn > Rp2bn floor).

calibration.note: cov_engine qc passes with no BLOCK. The +21.3pp EBITDA-margin jump is the FY2025 SG&A 125% to Q2-26 95.7% cost cut; 100% is a fair run-rate, D&A 18%, capex 2%, NWC 0, tax 0 are sourced. But the forecast is not calibrated to the June actual: FY2026E parent equity 75.06 and cash -6.99 versus actual 136.00 and 45.36 (the Rp56.5bn placement is omitted), and net debt reaches +Rp97.2bn by 2035 with net_borrowing 0. The 4.3x P/B rests on that uncalibrated equity.

signoff.notes: APPROVED (round 2). The SELL is accepted on a reproducible SOTP: gross parts Rp92.45bn — media/retail/IP residual book floor Rp64.74bn [S0], DGNS at the 27 Oct close of Rp288 on 95.3485m shares = Rp27.46bn [S16][S11], Traya at sourced cost Rp0.25bn [S5] — plus holdco net cash Rp25.36bn after 10x capitalised overhead, less the 30% mid-point holdco discount = Rp20.16/share, rolled at COE 11.85% to Rp22.55 [S0]. The media line is disclosed as a residual floor and an upper bound, not a mark; the listed stake is at market; the forecast balance sheet is kept out of valuation. Round-1 L1-L5 and red-team C1-C12 are all accepted and implemented, and I re-checked the load-bearing items against the archived sources (S0 line items, S5, S11, S16, S17, S18). QC round 2 is PASS/neutral; facts verify; draft lint PASS with the one benign methods-count warning. The call is not one-input-heroic in either direction: with the holdco discount removed the pre-discount NAV of Rp28.8/share is still far below the Rp78 price, and zeroing the media floor still leaves about Rp9/share, so SELL survives a two-sided stress. Batch bias: the CONGLOMERATES book is not one-sided (ADD/HOLD/SELL mix), so no shared-input tilt; FOLK is not a konglo and its only listed stake (DGNS) is uncovered, so no sibling mark is at issue. COE 11.85% is the batch low but is the house config default beta of 0.90, and the asset SOTP is insensitive to it. No consensus/broker contamination found; no positions, sizing or P&L. Publication conditions — non-substantive record/prose consistency only, to be cleared in place on this approved report before the gate (QC Q1-Q4; house precedent ABMM, 28 Oct 2026): Q1, reword the calibration.ebitda_margin justification so the 100% opex hold is a rounded-up hold above the observed 95.7% Q2 ratio, not that ratio [S0]; Q2, delete "HSC exclusion" from the holdco_discount basis — FOLK is not on the published HSC list [S17] — and rest the 30% mid-point on the factors the report states [S2][S10]; Q3, reword the other_nonop basis to unidentified non-operating swings excluded from the operating base, with the recurring-charge risk, not "one-off consolidation effects" [S0]; Q4, render the target at the precision of the expected return (the engine value, not the rounded display) or state the rounding, so Rp23 and -71.1% agree. Q5-Q8 are clarity/completeness notes with no publication risk. Not a return: none of these changes rating, target value, direction or any load-bearing number. One additional prose nit (desirable, not a condition): the investment-summary sentence that the market discount "widened, not narrowed, as the stock has collapsed" [S4] reads backwards against a price still about 2.7x NAV and should be rephrased; the correct direction is stated elsewhere.

bias.note: Round-2 re-audit after the Sector Lead return. The operating inputs are at or near the last actual and the H1-26 run-rate: revenue +2.0% FY2026E against an H1-26 rate of about Rp18.7bn annualised (flat), gross margin 52% vs 51.5% H1, capex 2% vs 0.6-1.3%, and no forecast-book multiple is used anywhere. Opex at 100% of revenue is a rounded-up hold above the 95.7% Q2-26 observed ratio (5.037/5.262, [S0]), conservative by about Rp0.8bn of EBITDA and irrelevant to the SOTP. The two marks that set the SOTP offset each other: the media/retail/IP estate is carried at the full parent-book residual of Rp64.7bn (55% of gross parts) despite negative EBITDA in every year since the 2023 listing (the generous side, disclosed as an upper bound, [S0]), while Traya Hydro sits at its Rp0.25bn related-party cost with two Cikarang data-centre water projects unbooked (the conservative side, no disclosed contract value, [S5][S6]). The DGNS stake is at the 27 October market close [S16] and the 30% holdco discount is the mid-point of the house 20-40% base rate [S2][S10]. No single unsourced input carries the call: the bull is still Rp26 against the Rp78 price (-67%). Direction neutral.

findings.finding: The assumptions qc_justification for calibration.ebitda_margin still says the FY+1 100% opex ratio 'is the observed run-rate'. The observed Q2-26 ratio is 95.7% [S0] and the report now correctly calls 100% a rounded-up hold above it; the justification contradicts the corrected prose and claims a run-rate the source does not carry.

The holdco_discount basis still cites 'HSC exclusion' as a reason for the 30% mid-point. C8 and S17 established that FOLK is NOT on the published HSC list, and the report deleted every HSC claim; the stale basis carries a false factor into the model record and could be read as the discount's support.

The other_nonop basis asserts that the Q1-26 and Q2-26 non-operating swings are 'one-off consolidation effects', cited to [S0]. S0 is the line-item datapack with no explanation, and the report says the Rp15.6bn Q2 charge is unidentified and may recur. The assumption states as fact what the report treats as an irreducible evidence gap.

The also-published target renders Rp23 (val.tp_final 22.5459) while the expected return -71.1% is computed on Rp22.55; at Rp23 the return is -70.5%. The target and the return are mutually inconsistent at display precision, which a first published record should not carry.

Judge NOTE (also round-1 Q6): the revenue-growth shocks are inert in the asset-based SOTP, so the bear/bull spread is the symmetric +/-10pp discount alone. Section 5 says 'mirrored shocks on the discount and on revenue growth' without saying the growth shock does nothing to a NAV.

Judge NOTE: the forecast net-debt line (Rp97.2bn by FY2035 with net_borrowing 0) is an operating-roll artifact that omits the January placement. The report already excludes the forecast balance sheet from valuation and liquidity.

Facts F1 (np_parent 2026Q1 = 14.82) and F3 (equity 2026Q1 = 137.8) carry group figures while their keys name parent-line items (datapack np_parent 15.23; parent equity 153.81). The prose labels both correctly ('net profit', 'group equity'), so nothing published is wrong, but the keys will mislead a later model use.

The holdco card's output contract asks for look-through earnings and leverage and a dividend-upstream coverage ratio. The report gives holdco net cash and states that no dividend is upstreamed, but does not present those two ratios. No rating effect.
